output.brief: The departures are concentrated in the Kestrel team, not the group as a whole. 8 of the 11 associates on Kestrel resigned, against 1 of 13 who were never on it. All 11 worked under the new partner, Dorian Faulk, and he is on no other matter. That means we can't yet tell whether the cause is the workload or his supervision, because the two are completely overlapping. The evidence points to both: surveys report unsustainable weekends and humiliating late-night corrections, and Faulk himself wrote in March that the team was stretched and he was keeping people late. Pay looks like a weak explanation: other groups sit at normal attrition, the target change applied to every group, and the pay complaint is a minor theme. I'm moderately sure about this, but not enough to pick a fix. I advise against the £12k group-wide payment and closing the review; it would likely miss the cause and leave Kestrel associates in place. Next: commission the £9k confidential external interviews, designed to separate supervision from workload, and start recording matter and supervising partner in attrition reports. Kestrel moves to drafting in January 2027, so the interviews are time-sensitive.
